newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls off crisis talks with miners' union.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls off crisis talks with miners' union.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday called off crisis talks planned for later in the day with miners angered at government plans to cut subsidies to the coal industry, Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said.

Bohl told reporters on the fringe of a cabinet meeting that the talks with miners' union boss Hans Berger had been called off because of the thousands of miners massing in Bonn to protest against the planned cuts.
Bohl said the negotiations would now take place on Thursday because "reasonable talks cannot be held in such a tense atmosphere".
Bonn's government quarter has been virtually besieged since Monday by angry pitworkers who fear more than half of them will lose their jobs as part of the government's latest move to save money.

Buses poured into Bonn all night from the mining districts of the Ruhr, Germany's ailing steel-and-coal heartland, and from Saar state on the French border. The union said it expected up to 20,000 to demonstrate in Bonn on Tuesday.
Some miners' representatives had been suggesting the demonstrations might turn violent unless Kohl offered concessions at the talks.
